title: A tab between `:` and an anchor does not indent the block mapping on the next line
notes: The tab separates the colon from the anchor (production 66 allows tabs as separation in a line). The anchor stands alone on its line, so the block mapping that follows starts on the next line and is indented by that line's own spaces; the tab is not part of its indentation. The anchor belongs to the inner mapping.

provenance.reference: A reader that remembered the tab as the indentation of the block collection on the next line and refused the input with a tab cannot indent a block collection.
